title: Access request heuristics and prioritization runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Create a concise, operational runbook that product, support, and solutions teams can use to triage non-bug enterprise admin/access requests (RBAC role changes, SSO/SAML onboarding, SCIM provisioning, org policy exceptions). The runbook should produce a deterministic priority score and recommended routing (self-serve, SE assist, security review, enterprise success) and include decision heuristics, example request templates, and telemetry signals to measure correctness.

Scope: In-scope are feature requests and configuration requests submitted via the intake form or support tickets that change org-level controls or privileged user access. Out-of-scope are production incidents, security incidents, and automation-level bugs (those should route to the incident/engineering flows).

Outcome: A one-page scorecard + a longer runbook doc (Confluence) + acceptance criteria and sample prompts to wire into the intake form and help center articles.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic scoring algorithm defined: inputs, weightings, and thresholds (low/med/high) for priority and routing.
Runbook contains concrete routing recommendations: self-serve KB, support triage, solutions engineering, security review, or exec approval.
Sample intake form fields and validation rules produced so product/CS can update the intake UI.
A telemetry plan that marks correctness (accepted routing vs actual downstream path) and a dashboard spec for false-positive/false-negative routing rates.
Stakeholder sign-off from Support, Solutions, Security, and Legal documented as comments in this ticket.
work_items: Define heuristics matrix (customer tier, change blast radius, data sensitivity, automation risk, requested timeline).
Draft scoring formula and map thresholds to routing buckets.
Write runbook prose and one-page scorecard PDF.
Create intake form field list and validation rules; produce example copy for help center.
Define telemetry events and dashboard tiles; hand off to observability team with event spec.
Run tabletop with Support and SE to validate decision edges; iterate based on feedback.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Created initial ticket. Background: multiple enterprise customers requested faster decisions for RBAC/SCIM/SSO changes; Support currently escalates many low-risk asks to SE. Goal is to reduce SE load by ~30% for routine access changes.

2026-03-03 - Liam O'Connor: Quick draft of inputs for scoring: customer_tier (free/pro/enterprise), affected_user_count, roles_impacted_count, affects_privileged_role (boolean), requires_data_exfil_controls_change (boolean), requested_completion_timing (immediate/rushed/standard), compliance_scope (PCI/HIPAA/none). Sharing for review.

2026-03-04 - Sofia Martinez (Security): Reviewed heuristics; proposed increasing weight for 'affects_privileged_role' and adding 'requires_security_review' flag for changes touching authentication or SCIM schemas. Also asked for 'security_review_required' to default true for any change that alters SSO/SAML certificate rotation or SCIM mappings that modify attribute-level permissions.

2026-03-05 - Diego Chen (Support): Shared anecdotal prioritization: most SE time is spent on role matrix design requests and multi-tenant SCIM onboarding. Suggested a 'template roles' checkbox in the intake form to capture intent and reduce back-and-forth.

2026-03-07 - Liam O'Connor: Iterated scoring formula. Trade-offs considered: conservative scoring reduces risk but increases manual reviews; aggressive automation reduces latency but raises security exposure. Proposal: two-tier thresholds — auto-approve for low-risk, expedited review for medium, mandatory security review + SE for high-risk.

2026-03-09 - Aisha Patel: Linked Confluence draft (see links) and asked Observability to prototype routing correctness dashboard. Security sign-off pending for the exact threshold values for 'privileged role' weight.
